title: Debt and Extraction
premise: Emrys Amberdale, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, discovers that her own voiceprint is the key to a black-site server in Jakarta holding the extraction protocols of a dead intelligence program — and her name in its inheritance ledger. Hunted by the program's surviving handlers, she must decide whether to sell, destroy, or claim the secret that explains why her father vanished and why her identity was manufactured. In the end she trades the ledger itself to buy the life of the one handler who protected her, walks away with nothing but the truth of who she really is, and burns the archive behind her.
about_author: Ivo Ishikawa is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments for firms he cannot legally name. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be forgettable.

chapters.title: The Rules Keep Changing
chapters.summary: Emrys Amberdale runs protection detail for a paranoid financier in London, enforcing rules that shift weekly. A routine biometric audit flags an anomaly: her voiceprint matches an access key on a foreign server. POV: Emrys. Beat: unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Her client, Halloran, tests her loyalty with a staged breach and offers a bonus to report on her own agency. She declines; he smiles like she failed anyway. POV: Emrys. Beat: isolation sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: At 3 a.m., Emrys's voice alone unlocks a Jakarta server mid-remote-diagnostic. A fragment loads: her childhood address, her father's service number, a word — EXTRACTION. The connection dies. POV: Emrys. Beat: vertigo; the past reaching through technology.

chapters.title: Halloran's Ledger
chapters.summary: Digging into Halloran's files for leverage, Emrys finds payments routed to a defunct program called Meridian — the same name on the server fragment. Someone at her agency redacted it hours before she looked. POV: Emrys. Beat: the rules were never meant to protect her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Her Father
chapters.summary: A stranger named Okafor intercepts her outside the office, claiming he served with her father in Meridian and that her voiceprint was designed, not inherited. He gives her a burner and vanishes when a gray sedan appears. POV: Emrys. Beat: hope curdling into manipulation.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: Emrys's agency suspends her pending a 'compliance review'; her apartment has been searched with surgical care. She realizes the audit flag wasn't an accident — someone wanted her unlocked. POV: Emrys. Beat: betrayal; the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Jakarta
chapters.summary: Using Halloran's travel accounts, Emrys flies to Jakarta and reaches the server site: a decommissioned consulate annex still drawing power. Inside, dust-free corridors and a biometric cradle waiting for her voice. POV: Emrys. Beat: dread and compulsion in equal measure.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: The archive opens: Meridian extracted assets — and children — from collapsing regimes, forging new identities. Emrys finds her own intake file, her father listed as handler, marked DEBT OUTSTANDING. POV: Emrys. Beat: grief reframed as design; she was made for this.

chapters.title: Okafor's Version
chapters.summary: Okafor reappears, admitting he triggered the unlock: dying, he needs the ledger sold to fund protection for other Meridian children. Emrys doesn't trust him but can't refute the file. POV: Emrys. Beat: reluctant alliance built on shared damage.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: A broker called Vess surfaces, offering seven figures for the full ledger — and revealing a rival bidder: Halloran, whose fortune was built on Meridian's laundering. POV: Emrys. Beat: the secret's price becomes concrete, obscene.

chapters.title: Halloran Arrives
chapters.summary: Halloran lands in Jakarta with his own contractors and a polite dinner invitation that is unmistakably a summons. Over dinner he tells her the debt is hers by blood and offers partnership instead of purchase. POV: alternating Emrys/Halloran. Beat: charm as a weapon.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Emrys plays both sides, feeding Vess a partial copy while stringing Halloran along, buying time to verify the ledger's second layer — a kill-list of unextracted children still active. POV: Emrys. Beat: cold competence masking panic.

chapters.title: The Second Layer
chapters.summary: Decrypted, the deeper archive shows the program never ended; it was privatized, and Halloran is its current owner. The kill-list is his pruning tool. POV: Emrys. Beat: moral clarity arriving too late to be comfortable.

chapters.title: Okafor's Debt
chapters.summary: Okafor confesses his role in her father's disappearance: her father tried to burn Meridian from inside and was extracted himself — erased, possibly alive. Okafor's sale was meant to find him. POV: Okafor. Beat: guilt, and the first true thing anyone has told her.

chapters.title: Compromise
chapters.summary: Vess learns the copy is partial and gives Emrys twelve hours or he sells her location to Halloran. Simultaneously, her agency formally terminates her, cutting her cover entirely. POV: Emrys. Beat: every exit narrowing at once.

chapters.title: What Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Emrys realizes the one secret worth killing for isn't the ledger — it's proof Halloran personally authorized erasures, enough to detonate his empire. She begins building the trade: the proof for her father's file location. POV: Emrys. Beat: resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: A night of tradecraft across Jakarta: dead drops, cloned drives, a near-miss with Halloran's contractors that leaves Okafor wounded. Emrys carries him rather than abandon him — breaking her own rule. POV: Emrys. Beat: loyalty chosen over survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: At the old annex, Emrys offers Vess the authentication key to the full ledger in exchange for passage out — but Halloran's team hits the meeting first. Vess flees with half the prize; gunfire collapses the corridor. POV: Emrys. Beat: chaos; plans dying faster than they're made.

chapters.title: Climax: Extraction Protocol
chapters.summary: Cornered in the archive room, Emrys uses the system against its owner: her voiceprint can execute a final protocol — total disclosure to every regulator, journalist, and family on Meridian's lists. Halloran begs; she speaks the activation phrase. POV: Emrys. Beat: the price paid — she can never be anonymous again.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Meridian's exposure goes global; Halloran is arrested trying to board a private jet. Okafor, stabilized, gives her a lead on her father — a name, a city, no promises. POV: Emrys. Beat: exhausted vindication without comfort.

chapters.title: Debt Outstanding
chapters.summary: Emrys tracks the lead to a coastal town and finds a man living under another name who may or may not be her father. He looks at her with recognition and fear, and asks who sent her. POV: Emrys. Beat: the inheritance question left open, painfully human.

chapters.title: Amberdale
chapters.summary: Emrys chooses not to force the reunion yet; some debts are paid by walking away. She takes a new contract under her real, recovered name and deletes her last backup of the ledger. POV: Emrys. Beat: quiet resolution — identity claimed, not given.
